manifesto.label: Manifesto
manifesto.title: Tools that respect the people who use them.
manifesto.body: Syria is rebuilding. Turkey is reinventing itself. The Arabic-speaking web is hungry for software that understands the language, the culture, and the constraints. I make AI tools that take that seriously — fast on slow networks, honest about their limits, useful before they're impressive.

about.label: About
about.title: Hello — I'm Hasan.
about.lede: I'm an AI engineer from Aleppo, based between Aleppo and Ankara. I build practical software for places the major platforms forgot about.

background.heading: Background
background.body: I grew up in Aleppo through years that didn't make it easy to study, ship, or stay. I learned to build software because there was no one around to build it for us. Most of what I know I taught myself, then verified with the people who used what I made.

now.heading: Now
now.body: I split my time between Ankara and Aleppo. I take on a small number of consulting engagements per year and spend the rest of my time on tools for Arabic-speaking users — RAG, on-device models, retrieval pipelines, and the very unglamorous plumbing that makes them reliable.

approach.heading: Approach
approach.body: Start with the person, not the model. Ship something narrow that works before something broad that doesn't. Be honest about latency, cost, hallucinations, and the limits of the language data. Document what you build so the next engineer doesn't have to start over.
